chunks: And from him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The fasting of three days as an expiation for an oath is consecutive, there cannot be a gap between them.
ai.seo_question: What is the requirement for the three days of fasting when expiating an oath in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi specifies that the three days of fasting required to expiate an oath must be consecutive (mutatabi'at) without interruption, a condition emphasized by Shia jurists to ensure the completeness of the expiation. It reflects the practical legal application of Quranic verses on oaths, highlighting the importance of continuity in fulfilling religious obligations to rectify verbal commitments.
